newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia truckers' union ends six-day strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombia truckers' union ends six-day strike.

text.p: A spokesman for Colombia's main truck drivers' union confirmed late Friday that it had agreed to end a six-day-old work stoppage with immediate effect.

Mario Quiroga, sectional chief of the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC) for central Boyaca province and member of its strike bargaining committee, said the strike order was lifted Friday afternoon.

The order was only given out after a decree, signed by President Ernesto Samper and Transportation Minister Carlos Hernan Lopez, gave official approval to accords worked out in a marathon bargaining session that ended early Friday after more than 22 hours of talks, Quiroga told Reuters.

The strike, which ACC leaders say virtually paralyzed all highway cargo, prevented the movement of coffee and other key exports to Colombia's three main ports and threatened to cause serious economic damage if it extended into next week.
Among other measures to end the work stoppage, which was declared illegal as of midnight Thursday, the government agreed to set minimum cargo rates for highway freight.
